item.title: How to Marry a Millionaire | Matinee Classics — Sun Nov 15, 4:00 PM — IU Cinema
item.description:
Three New York models—Shatze (Lauren Bacall), Pola (Marilyn Monroe), and Loco (Betty Grable)—set up in an exclusive apartment with a plan: tired of cheap men and a lack of money, they intend to use all their talents to snag three millionaires. The trouble is what happens when real love comes along? Co-starring William Powell in his second-to-last movie role, Cameron Mitchell, Rory Calhoun, Fred Clark, and David Wayne, How to Marry a Millionaire was the first comedy to be shot in CinemaScope and the second film to ever use the format. [95 min; comedy; English]
Source: Pillar Arts Community Calendar

item.title: It's On Us: Bystander Intervention Workshop — Mon Nov 16, 6:00 PM — Global & International Studies Building
item.description:
The It’s On Us: Bystander Intervention Workshop is a 90-minute, audience-driven bystander intervention program that teaches students the skills needed to help in situations involving alcohol and drug use that could lead to a sexual assault. Students practice helping in real-life scenarios and discuss how alcohol and drug use influences a person’s ability to give and get consent to engage in sexual activity with another person.
It's On Us is required for all first-year and transfer undergraduate students. You must attend one session to fulfill the requirement.
Instructions:
Those who arrive more than 5 minutes after the start time will NOT be allowed into the session and will need to attend a different session
If this is your assigned workshop but you cannot attend it in its entirety, please RSVP for a different workshop.
If you have concerns about attending due to personal experiences or need to request accommodations, please contact the office at itsonus@iu.edu.
A

item.title: Psychology Bingo Night — Thu Dec 3, 6:00 PM — Psychology
item.description:
Finals are coming, so take a study break that still counts as studying! Join Psychology Club for Psychology Bingo Night. Every bingo card is filled with psychology concepts and topics, from classical conditioning to cognitive dissonance. Mark them off as we call them out and see how much you remember. It’s a low-key way to relax, hang out with other psych students, and brush up on what you know before finals week. And yes, there will be prizes!
Hosted by: Psychology Club at Indiana University
Additional Information can be found at: https://beinvolved.indiana.edu/event/12981260
Source: IU beINvolved Student Orgs
